Messages.Author: Petri Wessman
Messages.Body:
A question came up in a game yesterday: if I bring out a Black Spiral
Buddy, and on the same turn turn him into an Abomination, can the new
Ab take an action that turn? The BSB cannot since he is a
newly-recruiteed ally, but the Ab is no longer an ally... does the
no-action-this-turn restriction still apply?

//Petri

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:


I don't think the restriction on first-turn ally actions applies. The
Abomination doesn't "remember" anything about it's past as an ally. And unlike
other cards, Abomination card text doesn't have any such restrictions
(Embracees need to hunt, Progeny and Creation Rites can't act). So card text
(or lack thereof) indicates that the Abomination can do whatever he wants when
created (unless he must hunt b/c he's empty).

Halcyan 2

Messages.Author: GreySeer
Messages.Body:
"Halcyan 2" <halc...@aol.com> wrote in message
news:20011030052236...@mb-fi.aol.com...


You cannot turn an ally into an Abomination in the turn the ally is
recruited because it doesn't enter your ready region until the end of your
influence phase [6.1.5]. When you do get to create the abomination, it can
act the turn it is created.

Allies are odd in this reguard, it is controlled but it is not ready (
somewhat similar to a vamp in torpor ) and hence can use it's special
abilities but cannot do anything, or be the target of an effect, that
requires the minion to be ready. Abomination requires the target to be ready
( card text ).
